newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS - POLAND'S HANDLOWY HEAVILY OVERSUBSCRIBED.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - POLAND'S HANDLOWY HEAVILY OVERSUBSCRIBED.

text.p: The privatisation offer of
Poland's Bank Handlowy was heavily oversubsubscribed in both
retail and institutional tranches with foreign demand exceeding
$3.5 billion, the issue's lead manager said on Wednesday.
Krzysztof Opawski, head of Schroders Polska, told a news
conference the offering was three times subscribed in the
retail offer and 17.4-times subscribed in the institutional
tranche.
He said the public offering, which the treasury priced late
on Tuesday at the top of the 28-35 zloty range, would bring into
the treasury's coffers about 1.3 billion zlotys.
Opawski said that Handlowy's public offer managed to lure
scores fo international financial institutions including some
newcomers.
"(International institutions) placed more than 600 bids
worth more than $3.5 billion and among those interested there
were investment funds and pension funds and for some
institutions it was their first investment in Poland," he said.
He said the biggest demand, 31 percent of the total, came
from the British market, with U.S. investors accounting for 26
percent of demand.
Bids from Polish institutional investors made up about two
percent of the total demand, he added.
Opawski said about 40 percent of foreign orders were placed
for Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) but the treasury ministry
decided to offer only 20 percent of the 19.5-million-share
institutional tranche in the form of GDRs.
Opawski said the retail offer originally set at 9.75
million shares or 15 percent of Handlowy's equity was increased
by 9.1 million taken out of a 27.86 million offer for so-called
stable investors to meet heavy demand.
Handlowy, which offered several incentives, including a
five-percent discount in the early stage of the subscription,
to lure as many retail investors as possible, attracted almost
140,000 bids in the retail tranche.
Opawski said that after the increase in the retail offer
demand was met in 65 percent on average.
He said that out of the total demand 92 percent came from
institutions and eight percent from individual investors.
Handlowy was offering a total of 61,750,000 shares out of
its 65 million shares with the public subscription held on May
26-June 13.
It is also offering up to 4,641,000 shares to its employees
at par value of four zlotys. The treasury ministry has yet to
sign final agreements on the sale of Handlowy shares with
long-term investors: JP Morgan, , Zurich Group and
Swedbank .
